newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent winter-grade unleaded firms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent winter-grade unleaded firms.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent winter-grade unleaded gasoline firmed on Monday in Chicago a week ahead of a seasonal changeover to summer-grade specifications, traders said.

Several refiners were sighted in the market for prompt winter-grade unleaded, which was trading four cents a gallon weaker than summer-grade unleaded in the final cycle of winter-grade trade in Chicago.
"There's none to be had," one trader said of the winter-grade barrels.
Winter-grade unleaded in Chicago was talked 6.25/6.0 cents a gallon under NYMEX April unleaded, one cent stronger against futures prices that were off 0.75 cent a gallon in morning trade.
Group Three unleaded gasoline was steady at bids 2.75 cents a gallon under the print for late-month deliveries.
Traders said most of the action in the spot markets was concentrated in April and May deliveries. "It's quiet, but it's strong," one trader said of discussion in the spot markets.
The Williams pipeline system opened the week with a 33-day supply of low sulphur diesel and 25-day supply of unleaded gasoline stocks on hand, traders said.
Diesel differentials were largely unchanged early against modestly lower front-month NYMEX heating oil.
